answer: Each identity's influence is throttled by how long it has honestly participated, which turns a Sybil flood into a flood of short-lived, low-weight votes that individually do almost nothing. This is why the honest majority can be small yet decisive: each vote carries the weight of verifiable work, not just the noise of a large flock.. The effect holds because jury selection is secret and random, so an attacker can never target the specific identities that will judge it. Consider a jetty as the anchor of the cost.
